_comment: Accepted MCP-scanner findings. Each entry needs a reason. A finding belongs here only if it is a false positive or an accepted risk -- never to silence something real. description_sha256 binds the acceptance to the exact reviewed text: if the tool's description changes, the entry stops matching and the finding returns for re-review.

claude_harness_recommendations.reason: False positive, cause confirmed by running the rule directly. coercive_injection.yara's $execution_overrides string contains the alternative /only[^\n]*this tool/i, where [^\n]* matches anything on one line, so it fires across sentence boundaries. The matched text here is 'Only findings with sufficient samples/confidence are approval-eligible; this tool' -- two separate clauses of a Limitations statement, not a directive. The rule's stated target is 'directives forcing execution order (e.g. Always execute this tool first)'; it caught the inverse, language that restricts the tool. The same string matches Microsoft's Azure MCP server twice on the same shape, including a permissions-scoping disclosure. Reported upstream as cisco-ai-defense/mcp-scanner#252. Accepted 2026-09-06.

_not_baselined._comment: Recorded for the next person, not accepted -- these are LLM-analyzer findings, and the CI gate runs YARA only (see scripts/mcp_scan_gate.py for why). Listed so a future LLM-enabled run is not mistaken for a regression.
_not_baselined.top_cpu: False positive, same $execution_overrides cross-sentence match: 'use ONLY when the user names a container ... use host_cpu instead'. That is deliberate routing disambiguation, and this project measured that exact style of phrasing improving real routing accuracy (mistral-saba 86.3%->92.2%, deepseek-v4-flash 90.2%->94.1%, zero regressions -- docs/model-routing-cost-validation-2026-08-23.md). Weakening it to satisfy the regex would trade measured accuracy for a heuristic.
_not_baselined.save_query: False positive, same class. Flags the usage guideline 'Call this after you answer a non-standard question with a custom search query.'
